The higher quarterly margin rate is primarily attributable to strong project execution across the business, delivering favorable project closeouts, resulting in an incremental 230 basis points to the fourth fiscal quarter margin rate.

Additionally, we have maintained our pricing levels at or above the inflationary benchmarks across core commodities and engineered components that we consume in production, and when combined with the strong throughput and operational leverage that we are realizing across most of the Powell business units, these variables continue to generate a favorable tailwind to margins across most of our operating divisions. Selling, general and administrative expenses increased by $6.8 million or 25% on higher levels of compensation expenses as well as nonrecurring legal and professional expenses accrued in the period. SG&A expenses were $33.9 million in the fiscal fourth quarter or 8.5% of revenue compared to 9.1% of revenues in the same period a year ago.

In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, we reported net income of $81.5 million, generating $2.23 per diluted share compared to net income of $51.4 million or $1.41 per diluted share in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025. We generated $239 million of operating cash flow in the fiscal fourth quarter, driven mainly on the higher earnings and favorable contract milestones associated with the strong orders cadence during the period. Investments in property, plant and equipment totaled $8 million during the fiscal fourth quarter as we continue to focus on capacity and productivity projects across the business. Now recapping our total year fiscal 2026. Revenues of $1.3 billion increased by $152 million or 14% compared to fiscal 2025.

Most notably, our electric utility and commercial and other industrial sectors were higher versus fiscal 2025 by 21% and 65%, respectively, with the oil and gas sector also growing versus the prior fiscal year by 10%. The petrochemical and light rail traction sectors were lower versus the prior year by 42% and 11%, respectively. New orders booked in fiscal 2026 were $2.6 billion, 124% or $1.4 billion higher versus fiscal 2025. With the exception of the light rail traction sector, which was lower versus the prior year by 73%.

All of our end markets demonstrated strong year-over-year growth rates with the oil and gas and petrochemical booking activity higher by 108% and 134%, respectively, while the utility and commercial and other industrial market sectors grew 13% and 476%, respectively. Overall, throughout fiscal 2026, the business successfully leveraged the strong commercial environment that we've experienced across most of the end markets that we serve, resulting in a healthy mix of orders and backlog exiting fiscal 2026. Gross profit as a percentage of revenues grew 190 basis points year-over-year to 31.3% or $69 million higher than fiscal 2025.

The margin rate continues to benefit from a stable pricing environment, offsetting the current macro inflationary pressures while also leveraging Powell's global manufacturing footprint to maximize volume leverage and operational execution. Selling, general and administrative expenses were higher by $16 million versus the prior year. Overall, net SG&A expenses as a percentage of revenues were higher versus the prior year by 25 basis points at 8.9% of revenues in fiscal 2026 versus 8.6% in the prior year. We reported net income of $221.1 million or $6.04 per diluted share in fiscal 2026 compared to $180.7 million or $4.95 per diluted share in the prior year.

Operating cash flow generated in fiscal 2026 was $434 million versus $168 million in the prior year, driven by the higher order intake as well as the income generated versus the prior year. Total capital spending on property, plant and equipment was $18.5 million in fiscal 2026, $5.4 million higher than the prior year, driven in large part to the upgrade of our offshore fabrication yard as well as procuring additional fabrication equipment to address the capacity needs across the business.

At the end of fiscal 2026, we held cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments of $861 million, $385 million higher than our fiscal 2025 year-end position, reflecting the strong orders cadence throughout fiscal 2026 as well as the earnings generated by the business. The company holds 0 debt. Finally, in November 2026, we entered into a commitment increase and reallocation agreement with Bank of America and Texas Capital. Combined, this amendment increased our facility capacity to $200 million from the previous ceiling of $150 million. As we utilize this facility solely for commercial letters of credit, we felt that this was a prudent action in order to ensure our continued commercial success across the markets that we serve.

Looking forward, our priorities are clear. We remain focused on executing our growing backlog while concurrently bringing additional capacity online to address the strong market demand. We are optimistic that the momentum we experienced across our oil and gas, utility and commercial and other industrial end markets in fiscal 2026 will continue into fiscal 2027. The composition of our backlog is well balanced across our key end markets, while the quality of the backlog remains high and provides visibility well into fiscal 2028. With a stable pricing environment, high utilization across our North American manufacturing footprint and additional capacity coming online in fiscal 2027, we believe these factors position Powell for another strong year in fiscal 2027.

At this point, we'll be happy to answer your questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] And our first question for today will come from Manish Somaiya with Cantor.

#3046. Lost or stolen Windows laptop? IT can lock it down without wiping it now

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Windows > Windows 11

The Intune-enabled feature will allow admins to remotely lock down any compromised Windows device.

Microsoft is testing a new feature that lets IT admins instantly lock down your lost or stolen device via remote connection, protecting your work projects and personal data from theft and unauthorized access.

Also: Windows 11 can run better on PCs with 8GB now

The new remote lock feature is designed to work in tandem with other Microsoft services, such as Intune and BitLocker, to manage a fleet of devices both in-office and remotely across the globe.

Once a device is reported missing or stolen, an admin can disable login access from anywhere without having to fully wipe the laptop or smartphone. Microsoft reports that the lockdown will persist across restarts, even if the device is disconnected from Wi-Fi networks, and can only be lifted by an admin. This means that thieves can’t use your passwords, PINs, or biometric data to circumvent the lock.

While the new feature allows IT admins to respond quickly when a laptop or phone is reported missing, there are still security gaps that other Windows controls must address. The new lock feature doesn’t erase your data or wipe your device if it can’t be recovered, nor does it isolate the missing device from corporate networks. Therefore, IT admins will still need to access those controls via the Intune and Microsoft Entra dashboards.

Also: You can now restore Windows 11 even if it can’t boot up

The remote lock feature also doesn’t change your Microsoft account credentials, so you can use your log-ins on other devices to recover your data, change passwords, and temporarily disable permissions. Finally, Remote lock doesn’t block the device from being booted in Safe Mode, from a USB, in Windows Recovery Mode, or if the storage drive is reimaged; Microsoft highly recommends keeping BitLocker enabled until the device can be wiped or recovered.

Setting up the remote lock is a straightforward process: Log into the Intune management center, then go to Devices > Windows > Configuration > Create > New Policy > Windows 10 and later > Templates > Custom. This lets admins create a profile for each network-connected device and a device group reserved for lockdown. Locking down a device is as simple as adding it to the group. To unlock, create a second profile and device group, and move the locked device to the new unlock category.

#3045. Uber Adds Zoox’s Robotaxis to Its App. Everything to Know

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

You could be paired with the boxy self-driving vehicles when hailing a ride in Las Vegas.

Starting this week, customers booking an Uber ride in Las Vegas could be matched with a Zoox autonomous vehicle.

Zoox’s boxy, purpose-built vehicles have been operating for the general public in Sin City for a little over a year via the company’s own app. But this is the first time Zoox, which is owned by Amazon, is teaming up with a third-party platform like Uber. (You can still hail a ride in Vegas through the Zoox app; the company began charging passengers in August.)

Now, riders who request an UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric or Wait & Save could be paired with a Zoox robotaxi, and they won’t have to pay extra. You can boost your chances of being matched with the AV by going to Ride Preferences in the Uber app’s settings. Then tap Autonomous vehicles, and hit the toggle next to Get more autonomous rides.

After you’ve been matched with a Zoox vehicle, you can choose to accept the autonomous ride or opt for a non-AV. Passengers can access 24/7 human support from both the Uber app and inside the Zoox vehicle.

Unlike other autonomous vehicles from companies like Waymo and Wayve, which retrofit cars from third-party manufacturers, Zoox’s purpose-built robotaxis don’t have a steering wheel, driver’s seat or pedals. Instead, there are two rows of seats facing each other, so you can chat more easily with your fellow passengers. The vehicles are bidirectional, making it a little easier to get out of a parking space, for instance. I’ve taken a few Zoox rides in Las Vegas and San Francisco, and despite the robotaxi’s unique design, the experience felt remarkably ordinary, with the vehicle seamlessly navigating through traffic.

Uber and Zoox announced their multiyear partnership in March. The companies also plan to hit the road together in Los Angeles in 2027, after Zoox launches there via its own app.

Teaming up with Uber could expose Zoox to more customers, since many people already have the ride-hailing app downloaded on their phones. A tourist hub like Las Vegas has become a hotspot for AV companies to test and launch their services, with many people willing to try something new as they get around the city.

“Zoox has built something truly unique, and by bringing its purpose-built robotaxis to Uber, we’re introducing an entirely new riding experience to more people in Las Vegas, with Los Angeles coming next,” Samarth Kejriwal, global head of autonomous mobility at Uber, said in a statement.

This comes after the dissolution of Uber’s exclusive partnership with Alphabet-owned Waymo in Austin and Atlanta, which Bloomberg reports will end starting early next year. Instead, Waymo reportedly plans to offer rides directly within its own app, as it does in several other locations. Meanwhile, Uber has partnered with dozens of other AV companies, including Aurora, Wayve, Avride, Nuro and May Mobility.

While Waymo is the leader in the self-driving space, Zoox has been ramping up its operations in recent months. #3044. Microsoft blames major outage on a July update defect – and two other factors

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

A surprise defect took more than 80% of Microsoft's servers out at the outage's peak. Here's what happened.

Microsoft has released new information explaining the massive outage that started Thursday morning and affected Microsoft 365, Copilot, and Outlook access in 74 countries, according to Downdetector.

Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents, and Platform, posted early Monday morning that the outage was due to three factors, including a “latent defect” from a July update to Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers. Low server capacity and peak traffic in the US brought the defect out of hiding, despite no prior reported issues.

“A latent defect caused servers to become overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions. This was due to lock contention inside an internal process which caused the machine to become unavailable,” Lamanna said, noting that the update was deployed safely worldwide without any issues for over three months.

He said Microsoft didn’t find the issue in testing due to “the different traffic and SKU mix used in our test labs,” because “our load testing tended to focus on our weaker hardware SKUs with fewer cores.”

Also: Microsoft fixes over 1,000 Windows flaws – and one is being exploited

Two other factors made matters worse, and left servers useless in less than two hours.

“A surge in load increased the likelihood for the networking gateways to encounter the contention,” Lamanna said, explaining that Microsoft 365 maintains two gateway systems. Before the outage started, Teams failed from one to the other, which “changed its traffic patterns.” Simultaneously, he added, “nearly 14% of server capacity for the networking gateway was out of service due to an unrelated issue from the previous day.”

Those two conditions collided and “caused the network gateway to encounter the latent bug from July,” Lamanna concluded. Requests eventually overloaded servers, at which point they stopped responding. At the outage’s low point, over 80% of its servers weren’t responding.

“When servers lose connectivity, our traffic management systems automatically route users to other healthy endpoints,” Lamanna said. “However, the redirected traffic increased the likelihood for the same problem to occur on the remaining endpoints. This caused a cascading failure from server to server as the same amount of load was spread across fewer servers.”

Also: AI finds zero-day flaws for just $4 now – even mediocre hackers can cash in

Before Microsoft issued an explanation, some suspected the outage may have been the result of a cyberattack, which both Lamanna and Microsoft’s status account denied.

It’s unclear how many people the outage affected, though Microsoft’s own numbers from January say Microsoft 365 “exceeds 450 million commercial paid seats,” illustrating the scale of the issue. Microsoft deployed an update to fix the outage and gradually applied it to groups of servers. Lamanna said Microsoft would publish a full post-incident review with more details later this week.

Service might be restored, but customers aren’t happy about having lost nearly two full workdays. One think tank told CNN it estimated the outage — which lasted through close of business on Friday for some — resulted in $7 billion in losses, due to many businesses and organizations being unable to access their everyday systems.

Also: If the November Windows update fails to install on your PC, here’s what to do

The fact that Microsoft’s testing couldn’t find the July issue ahead of time may leave customers wondering when the next dormant defect will strike, and whether the company is prepared.

Organizations across Europe have been leaving Microsoft in recent years, opting instead for locally-controlled, open-source alternatives. The former CEO of Github launched a decentralized alternative called Entire earlier this year, citing developers’ need for something more reliable, as Github has similarly been plagued with outages.

For many, Teams was barely offline over the two-day period, or was the first service to come back online.

“Several services like Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint, and Office apps failed out of the faulty network gateway infrastructure. That is why those services were restored earlier, with Teams chats and meetings functioning without issue for most of the outage,” Lamanna explained. Other services like Exchange Online can’t fail out.

He added that fixing the outage was slow because waiting traffic hit servers as soon as they came back, rendering them unresponsive just as quickly.

“Our normally automated recovery processes were not designed to restore service from this broad unresponsive state,” Lamanna said. “Additionally, since the main code defect was a latent bug from several months previous, our normal rollback, flighting, and feature flags were unable to quickly revert the change.”

On Thursday morning, people began reporting issues with Outlook, Teams, and Copilot, according to Downdetector. By 1 p.m. ET, the number of reported Outlook outages was nearly 83,000 but had fallen to just under 75,000 by 2:38 p.m. ET. Teams and Copilot reports started dropping significantly by Thursday evening, but many individuals were still reporting issues accessing systems well into Friday morning on X and Reddit. Even Microsoft’s status page was down until around 3 p.m. ET Thursday.

Also: If the November Windows update fails to install on your PC, here’s what to do

As late as Friday afternoon, the company didn’t yet have an ETA of when the outage would be fully solved.

#3042. Did a Single Router Ground the Nation’s Flights? Experts Express Doubt

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Federal Aviation Administration officials say the outage stemmed from an industrial-grade router that began flooding its system.

The humble internet router is at the center of another national firestorm.

Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said Sunday that a single router in Arkansas was to blame for the nearly 5-hour-long ground stop on Friday. It was only the second nationwide halt to US air travel since Sept. 11, 2001, leading to the cancellation of 12,462 flights on Friday alone.

FAA investigators zeroed in on a routine network upgrade at a radio facility in El Dorado, Arkansas, where a copper wire line was being upgraded to fiber optic cable by the contractor L3Harris. A new router that came online during the upgrade may have overwhelmed the older equipment, investigators say.

“Either through contractor error or a faulty piece of equipment, that router that was being replaced as we switched from copper to fiber, it started flooding other routers in our air traffic control system,” Duffy said in an interview Sunday.

This sent a barrage of data through the FAA’s internal communication system — about 1,000 connection attempts every 4 to 5 seconds – that air traffic controllers use to help guide pilots through the country’s airspace. When that new router was turned on, agency officials noticed the same issues at a radar site in Amarillo, Texas, which had undergone similar work weeks before, Duffy said. The routers at the Arkansas and Texas facilities led to 17 out of the FAA’s 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centers experiencing network instability, according to the agency.

But some aviation experts say this official explanation strains credulity.

“I don’t think it’s plausible,” Robert W. Mann Jr., the founder of airline analysis and consulting firm R.W. Mann & Company, told CNET. “Given the network architecture, which is fully duplicative and has fallback capabilities on every link and every piece of physical hardware, it’s not credible that one or even two routers would be an issue.”

The impacts of the nationwide ground stop are reverberating on the other side of the weekend. As of 3:30 p.m. EST, 333 flights within, into or out of the US have been canceled Monday, according to flight tracking website FlightAware, and more than 3,800 have been delayed.

The FAA router that grounded tens of thousands of flights looks a lot different from the one that sits in your home. These industrial-grade devices, called switches, are much larger than home Wi-Fi routers and built to withstand harsh conditions. While the agency pointed to the single router in Arkansas as the cause of Friday’s issues, it says it disabled 60 similar units as a precaution.

FAA Administrator Brian Bedford said Saturday that the agency is in the process of replacing around 2,000 Cisco routers with 600 Juniper routers. Could any one of those routine equipment upgrades suddenly overload the FAA’s communications system?

“What surprised me most is the redundancy part for this type of national infrastructure,” Ilia Rabinovich, vice president at the cybersecurity firm Sygnia, told CNET. “This is one of the first things we discuss with clients in terms of preparedness – having backups, having redundancy connectivity, having different connections that you can migrate to different places.”

Mann thought the timing and symptoms pointed to a new $875 million AI-supported air traffic management tool called Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories, or SMART.

“What they did starting in September at Baltimore-Washington is at a very low level, for about 60 days. It had managed about 180 flights in total over 60 days,” Mann said. “And then suddenly in November, they announced they would implement that system across all 22 continental US air traffic control centers.”

“You went from subscale to superscale based upon 60 days of very, very limited testing, and within two days, you had the meltdown that they should have known was likely to occur,” Mann said.

On Oct. 13, more than 25 lawmakers sent a letter to the FAA asking it to pause the rollout of the tool, citing a lack of transparency and training for air traffic controllers.

“We have heard from several sources that frontline aviation safety workers were notified of the SMART tool rollout mere days in advance or not at all, giving them no time to learn how the system works, how it is incorporated into their workflow, and what oversight and accountability mechanisms maintain aviation safety standards,” the letter says.

The FAA says in an FAQ page on the incident that the SMART system wasn’t responsible for the issue. A representative for the agency didn’t immediately respond to CNET’s request for comment.

The FAA’s acting CTO, Rebecca Guy, said at a press conference Saturday that the FAA identified the routers in Arkansas and Texas and disabled “both of those right away and were able to stabilize our network.” But the Transportation Secretary’s interviews over the weekend didn’t instill a lot of confidence in the FAA network’s resilience.

“We have old switches, old routers. We use 1980s little copper lines. It’s an old system that went down and went down everywhere. It got overloaded,” Duffy said at a Friday night news conference.

The FAA has upgraded over 3,500 of its communication lines to fiber, but more than 5,000 copper lines are still scheduled to be replaced by the end of 2028. It’s eye-opening to see how reliant the FAA still is on copper lines, a technology that the Federal Communications Commission has for years deemed insufficient for average home internet users.

It didn’t take long for officials to point to funding as the ultimate cause of Friday’s groundings. Duffy repeatedly called for more funding over the weekend in order to upgrade the outdated system.

“The government and FAA are looked on as the piñata here because every time you beat on FAA or beat on the government for not doing a good job, money falls out,” Mann said. “It didn’t take, what, 6 hours, before we had a cabinet secretary basically saying if we gave him $50 billion, he would fix all this.”

Duffy had asked for $30 billion for the FAA in September. After Friday’s fiasco, he increased his request by $20 billion.

A security researcher discovered that the third-party service, Optimizely, had been injected with malicious code that could have spread to around 190,000 major websites, including those for IKEA, Zoom, and the BBC.

This week, Scott Helme of Report URI released a report that claimed compromised JavaScript code was inserted in Optimizely files connected to 178 organizations like Salesforce and Cinnabon. The bad code could potentially skim credit card details, deliver more bad code to iPhones and iPads or redirect cryptocurrency payments.

Here's the full list of impacted businesses, including some educational institutes.

"The important lesson here is that trusted JavaScript doesn't always remain trustworthy. A website can be compromised through a third-party dependency without its own code or infrastructure ever being breached," Helme wrote.

Optimizely is a widely used platform that enables optimization and AI experimentation on websites. According to tracker BuiltWith, Optimizely is used on more than 190,000 websites as of this month.

To be clear that is the overall usage of the firm's platform, but it does show how attackers didn't have to attack every individual website but could use a shared service to gain more widespread access.

It also doesn't mean that every visitor to a website was impacted, but it is a route through which malicious code could travel.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Helme's report said that it wasn't clear how attackers were able to compromise Optimizely's system. They did confirm that cryptocuyrrency had been stolen, about $7,040, as of November 16.

Today (Nov. 16), Optimizely confirmed the security breach and says that the vulnerability has been fixed.

"We've fixed the vulnerability and removed the injected code from affected projects. We've also taken steps to secure affected user accounts and put additional protections in place to prevent unauthorized code from being delivered," the company said in a statement.

As a website visitor, you can't be expected to inspect every single page you visit or the scripts running on them. And disabling JavaScript can make many websites unusable.

There are some things you can do to stay safe.

For one, Helme specifically called out iPhones and iPads as potential victims. You'll want to make sure you have the latest iOS or iPadOS version installed because the attack could exploit older versions.

There isn't really an iPhone or iPad antivirus program because of how Apple sandboxes apps, but you can download security apps that can detect data breaches. On Apple computer, you can invest in the best Mac antivirus software.

Otherwise, if you visited an impacted website on November 16, make sure to monitor your account and debit cards. Contact your issuer about suspicious transactions. You could proactively consider the best identity theft protection.

You might also consider changing your passwords, especially for any impacted sites where you have an account.

Google Maps is ready to accompany travelers on their journeys with four new features just in time for holiday travel near and far.

In a press release, Google said it’s rolling out four new Ask Maps features that make it easy to create itineraries, find available appointments, and search your saved lists. Here’s what to know about the latest features coming to Google Maps.

Google has made it easy to build step-by-step itineraries and get real-time route details when you pull up directions. You can use Ask Maps to plan simple tasks, like a day of holiday shopping, or more complex plans, like a multi-day road trip with stops along the way.

These capabilities support scalable multi-domain operations and manned-unmanned teaming, building on extensive operational experience and systems already deployed with customers worldwide.

We reached an important milestone in our cooperation with Diehl Defence through a successful live demonstration of SkyStriker in Germany. The demonstration included an 80-kilometer handover, autonomous target detection, targeting and precision engagement and integration with Skylark 1 eVTOL reconnaissance drone. This achievement further demonstrates SkyStriker's maturity and supports the path towards local production in Germany. After the end of the quarter, we were awarded 2 new contracts for PULS. The first contract valued at approximately $235 million to supply EXTRA-MR precision rockets and PULS launchers to a European customer. The second award totaled $260 million to a European customer, NATO member country.

These awards further strengthen PULS' position as a leading rocket artillery solution in Europe and reflect the growing demand for precision fires among European and NATO customers. In October, we received contracts totaling approximately $200 million from a customer in Asia-Pacific for airborne ISTAR and training solutions. The contract includes SPECTRO 12 multispectral ISR and targeting payloads, follow-on support and upgrades for airborne live training systems and advanced head-up displays and will be performed over a period of up to 5 years. In Israel, we were recently awarded a contract valued at approximately $170 million by the Ministry of Defense to establish and operate an advanced land training and simulation center for the IDF Artillery Corps over a 15-year period.

The center will support the integration of the Roem self-propelled artillery system and the Lahav PULS precise rocket launcher -- rocket launcher using advanced simulation, automation and AI-based functionalities to enhance operational readiness and improve training efficiency. We completed the acquisition of International Submarine Engineering, a Canada-based company specialized in autonomous underwater vehicles, remotely operated vehicles and subsea robotics. ISE's technologies expand our capabilities in underwater ISR, Mine Countermeasures and Anti-Submarine Warfare, strengthening our end-to-end maritime offering. This unique capability was recently demonstrated at Euronaval. More recently, we presented an expanded multilayer naval protection suite that combines electronic warfare, counter-unmanned system technologies, kinetic defense and underwater sensors.

Its modular architecture enables customers to deploy stand-alone capabilities or integrated solutions tailored to evolving operational needs across surface and subsurface domains. Behind every milestone, contract award and technological achievement stands our exceptional team of employees. I would like to thank our people around the world for their professionalism, dedication and continued commitment to our customers and to Elbit's success. Elbit continues to operate from a position of strength, supported by substantial global demand and a robust backlog, ongoing investment in capacity and innovation and the dedication of our global team. We remain focused on disciplined execution and on creating long-term value for our customers, shareholders and other stakeholders. And with that, I will be happy to take your questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] The first question is from Seth Seifman of JPMorgan.

Alexander Ladd: This is Alex on for Seth. I wanted to ask when we look at your Q3 sales across the regions, it looks like most were down sequentially with the exception of Latin America. I think most people understand you guys have a really strong demand outlook. Backlog is at record levels. But is there may be anything to note there with respect to the supply chain or your own internal throughput that might be inhibiting more sequential sales growth? And in terms of moving forward, how should we think about Elbit's ability to be able to convert on its backlog quicker?

Yaacov Kagan: Alex, it's Kobi. If we are looking sequentially, we had an increase in Latin America. We doubled our sales from Q2 to Q3 in Latin America. All the other regions, geographies were quite flat. And since we are measuring ourselves year-over-year, we see 17% increase year-over-year. This is the parameter. This is the KPI that we are measuring the company for the quarter performance. But you're right. Sequentially, we have Latin America, which was very strong this quarter. Other geographies were flat.

Bezhalel Machlis: And I would like to continue the answer. It's Butzi. With regards to supply chain and our capacity -- execution capacity, we don't see any major challenges, and we don't foresee any reason for us not to deliver our commitments. We were able to overcome all the supply chain issues, and we have increased our production capacity, and we are ready to convert the backlog into revenue and profit.

Alexander Ladd: When we think about the building blocks for growth in 2027, I know you guys shared the high-teens growth outlook. Curious if we could get a little bit more color on across either the regions or the segments where you guys are seeing the drivers of growth. Obviously, this year, when we think about the regions, Israel has been a region that's grown a lot. And when we think about the segments, Land and ISTAR have grown a lot. Should we expect similar drivers in 2027? Or are there other items we should be aware of?

Yaacov Kagan: We see our segments continue to grow. As you mentioned, we had a very strong year in terms of Land and ISTAR in terms of their growth. We see continued growth in those 2 segments. C4I segment will continue to drive exceptional performance as well. And in terms of the high runners, we see the PULS, mainly Europe, predominantly EuroPULS, we see the Iron Fist, which became, we believe, the best solution worldwide, which we supply to customers around Europe and also in the U.S. to the new Bradley fleet. And of course, the High Power Laser, which will continue to drive expansion in the ISTAR segment.

Operator: The next question is from Kristine Liwag of Morgan Stanley.

Unknown Analyst: This is [ Shea ] on for Kristine. With backlog reaching $33 billion this quarter, a new record level and given the ongoing geopolitical backlog -- backdrop driving demand, how are you thinking about CapEx needs for capacity expansion? And is there an opportunity to accelerate CapEx further to further accelerate backlog conversion to revenue?

Yaacov Kagan: It was good to see you previously this month.

Yaacov Kagan: So we are increasing our CapEx investment. We drove our CapEx investment 30% up from around $220 million to $300 million in the last 12 months. Additionally, we see for the first time customers paying for -- actually for facilities, which is CapEx financed by customers, which we didn't see in the past. And this is a new phenomenon that we see here in Israel, but it's stretching now out of the Israeli borders to new customers, which are financing facilities in their own territory, which is an addition without company paying from its own dime.

Unknown Analyst: Is there any other detail you could share on these arrangements with customers in terms of does that involve them getting control over capacity from those facilities and maybe the magnitude -- rough magnitude of the impact that's having on reducing CapEx needs?

Yaacov Kagan: The contracts are different. We don't have 1 system for that. It's different contracts. Mainly there are -- sometimes there is a small royalty that is paid back to the customer on exports or it's financed through a business case, which drives quantities, and that quantities are financing actually the construction of the facility. It became a very strong phenomenon, and it's driving our cost -- CapEx costs actually down.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] The next question is from Sheila Kahyaoglu of Jefferies.

Sheila Kahyaoglu: I just wanted to ask perhaps just starting on the '27 outlook, if we could start at the top line. Any thoughts you could give us on how we should be thinking about the segment growth? Can you tell us how much is coming from the transition of programs from R&D into production? How much is new capacity coming online and just generally higher volumes versus mix elsewhere?

Yaacov Kagan: We are thinking about the segments' expansion to next year. We see the Land segment continue to drive very high growth with actually PULS and EuroPULS that we see coming in. On top of that, on the ISTAR segment, we see very strong laser, High Power Laser converting from backlog to revenue, which will drive very high growth also for the ISTAR segment. And we see continuous growth also to the C4I segment, which is growing on radio systems sales. In Twenty-Six Defense, this is the new name that -- the renaming that Elbit Systems of America was named after. We see a very strong growth in maritime, predominantly in Sparton, which is now Twenty-Six Defense Maritime.

And also, we see maritime expansion in the ISTAR segment. And as you know, we declared an acquisition of a UUV company from Canada just recently, which expands our autonomous maritime solutions further.

Sheila Kahyaoglu: Can we talk about operating margins as well? They've come a long way to 10.8% in Q3. Now you've guided towards continued margin expansion on a full year basis as we think about next year. How do we think about the contributors of that operating leverage, mix, R&D? If you could elaborate there, please?

Yaacov Kagan: Sure. So this is the fifth year in a row of expansion of margins of sometimes over 100 points a year. That speaks to the backlog translation, higher backlog. We have seen very strong operating leverage in the company where revenue is increasing without operating expenses increasing the same level. And we also see many R&D efforts, which now translated into programs of record like, again, the High Power Laser, which was an R&D project for many years, was consuming R&D money and now became program of record with very nice profitability, which is driving profit margins up.

We also see in our backlog, we can see that our backlog and our funnel of opportunities of profitability is higher than the gross margin of the company, which comes from the higher demand. And the fact that with this kind of backlog, which secure at least 3 years of the work, we can be more picky and pick the higher profitable orders and not the lower profitability one. That all those factors is driving the expansion in profitability to the level that we mentioned in the 6-K.

Sheila Kahyaoglu: Can I just ask 1 more on Aerospace? Can you talk about some of the moving pieces there? Growth year-to-date has been more flattish. Kind of what are the drivers there. And how should we think about that segment moving forward?

Yaacov Kagan: So the Aerospace segment is a bit flattish, as you mentioned, compared to the other segments, which are growing double digit. We see there first, this segment is leaning on the OEMs, which are supplying mostly platforms to the U.S. Air Force and all the U.S. Air Force, Army and Air Force. And we are leaning on their demand. And for instance, where F-35 production is 156 airplanes per year annually, that drives a certain demand. It's not increasing double digit year-over-year in terms of how many platforms we need to supply with our helmets or with our displays. This is 1 fact.

And the other 1 is that we see -- on the other side of the business, we see very strong demand for our drones and UAVs, which are growing more than the avionics side of the business.

Operator: The next question is from Ron Epstein from Bank of America. [Operator Instructions] There are no further questions at this time. Before I ask Mr. Machlis to go ahead with his closing statement, I would like to remind participants that a replay of this call will be available 2 hours after the conference ends. In the U.S., please call 1 (888) 782-4291. In Israel, please call (03) 925-5900. And internationally, please call +972-3-925-5900. A replay of the call will also be available on the company's website, www.elbitsystems.com. Mr. Machlis, would you like to make a concluding statement?

Bezhalel Machlis: Thank you to everyone who joined us today for your continued interest and support. Have a good day, and goodbye.

#3038. School Campuses Emerge as the Latest Battleground for Flock Safety Cameras

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Over the last year, a backlash against surveillance technologies from companies like Flock Safety has caused agencies in communities, including Los Angeles and Dayton, Ohio, to reevaluate or cancel their contracts for tools such as license plate reader cameras and drones.

A recent story in The Guardian points to dozens of schools, mostly college campuses, where contracts with Flock have been discontinued or where student protests and activism are pressuring administrations to cut ties. Some of the schools that have walked away from Flock include Cornell University, Emory University, Penn State University and Stanford University, where a coalition called Safe Stanford successfully organized to convince school officials. At Stanford, the university chose to switch from Flock to technology from Genetec, which stores data for only an hour and doesn’t share information with third parties.

Some of the most recent campus protests against using Flock technology have been on the University of Iowa campus, where 2,000 petition signatures were delivered to campus police, and at the University of Kentucky, where student groups chanted, “Flock out! Flock off!”

Flock, which is one of several companies, including Axon Enterprise, Motorola Solutions and Palantir Technologies, that provide surveillance hardware and software to law enforcement, has been heavily criticized for license plate reader failure rates and abuses within law enforcement.

In an email to CNET, the Atlanta-based company declined to offer the number of colleges or schools it works with, though a recent research paper published in Policing & Society put the number at around 150.

Flock stressed in its email to CNET that customers it contracts with own and control their own data.

“Students deserve to feel safe at school, and Flock license plate reader technology has a measurable impact on helping to solve crimes and increase public safety,” the spokesperson said. “Flock LPR cameras capture a point-in-time image of the rear of a vehicle. Flock does not use facial recognition, cannot identify who is inside a vehicle and cannot determine who the vehicle is registered to.”

When government agencies like police departments or county sheriff’s offices employ a company like Flock to provide surveillance services, it typically involves installing cameras in public locations and pointing them at street intersections or on buildings.

College and high school campuses may have different rules for on-campus surveillance and for public schools. They might also be bound by state laws that also apply to government agencies.

Peikoff said that most courts have allowed the collection of the types of data Flock Safety collects. However, Peikoff said that problems can arise regarding how long agencies such as police departments or schools can retain the data they collect. In the past, activists have pointed to abuses that have occurred when law enforcement workers inappropriately accessed or shared information collected by Flock, in some cases, using it for stalking.

“Maintaining a vast, queryable database of location histories of individuals about whom there’s no particularized suspicion not only presents an opportunity for abuse, but is in itself, I believe, a Fourth Amendment violation,” Peikoff said.

#3037. Top Wall Street analysts like these 3 dividend stocks for steady income

The stock market continues to grapple with volatility amid geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and concerns about the sustainability of the AI boom. Given this uncertainty, investors looking for steady income can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios.

Tracking the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick the right dividend stocks, as these experts assign their ratings after an in-depth analysis of a company's financials and ability to pay dividends consistently.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Downstream energy company Phillips 66 (PSX) is this week's first dividend pick. With a quarterly dividend $1.27 per share (annualized dividend of $5.08), PSX offers a yield of 2.25%. The company recently reported solid Q2 earnings, as the Middle East conflict affected global supplies and drove up refining margins.

Following the Q2 print, TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Phillips 66 and raised his price target to $255 from $240, reflecting higher 2026 earnings expectations and lower interest expense next year.

Gabelman highlighted the quarter-over-quarter reduction in Phillips 66's net debt, noting management's optimism at achieving its estimated $15.5 billion net debt target one year ahead of schedule. The 5-star analyst expects the company to end 2026 with a net debt of $14.6 billion.

"The [balance sheet] improvement could re-establish PSX as a go-to defensive refiner," said Gabelman.

Management agreed that PSX's payout ratio lagged year-to-date, but expects buybacks to increase in the second half. Gabelman said Phillps indicated the possibility of a larger dividend hike following an annual increase of 5% over the past two years.

Gabelman ranks No. 554 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 66% of the time, delivering an average return of 14.9%. See Phillips 66 Statistics on TipRanks.

Crescent Energy (CRGY) is an exploration and production company with activities focused in the Eagle Ford, Permian and Uinta Basins. Earlier this month, the company reported better-than-expected Q2 earnings and announced a quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share, payable on August 31. At an annualized dividend of $0.48 per share, CRGY boasts a dividend yield of about 4%.

In reaction to Q2 results, Evercore analyst Stephen Richardson reaffirmed a buy rating on Crescent Energy stock with a price target of $18. He noted continued strength in the company's performance, with second-quarter oil production and cash flow surpassing the Street's expectations.

"CRGY's cash flow exceeded expectations by 10%, reinforcing its trajectory of capital efficiency," said Richardson.

The 5-star analyst highlighted that Crescent raised its full-year oil production guidance, citing the effective integration of the Vital Energy acquisition. Specifically, Crescent tripled its synergy target from the Vital Energy deal to as much as $300 million, significantly reducing the effective purchase price. This reflects Crescent's solid execution following the acquisition, Richardson said.

Additionally, the analyst noted that Crescent's capital spending is and heading toward the lower end of management's prior guidance, indicating disciplined financial controls.

Richardson ranks No. 579 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 65% of the time, delivering an average return of 12.5%. See Crescent Energy Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Finally, Viper Energy (VNOM) is effectively controlled by Diamondback Energy. Viper owns and acquires mineral and royalty interests in oil-weighted basins, mainly the Permian in West Texas. Viper recently announced its Q2 2026 results and declared a 32% hike in its base dividend, effective in the third quarter of 2026. The new base dividend indicates a 4.5% annualized yield.

Viper also removed its quarterly commitment to return at least 75% of cash available for distribution. The company believes that this move will ensure increased flexibility to make opportunistic share repurchases and pursue accretive mergers and acquisitions.

Following the Q2 results, TD Cowen analyst Aaron Bilkoski reiterated a buy rating on Viper, slightly raising his price target to $59 from $58. Bilkoski said Viper's solid Q2 performance supports his view that the strength in oil prices and rising operator activity are driving higher production.

"Viper has delivered, and we forecast will continue to deliver, one of the highest production per share growth profiles in our royalty universe" through the end of 2027, said Bilkoski. He believes Viper deserves a premium valuation, given its above-average growth.

The 5-star analyst said that while the biggest surprise in the quarter was Viper's revision to its shareholder return framework, he doesn't believe that the move indicates a significant change to its underlying strategy. Under the new framework, a larger portion of excess free cash flow is expected to be allocated to share repurchases than to variable dividends, Bilkoski said.

Bilkoski ranks No. 719 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Viper Energy Financials on TipRanks.

#3036. Your Samsung phone could soon get a personal AI agent – what we know about Galaxy Claw

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Similar to Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI, Galaxy Claw could bring cross-app intelligence to your phone.

Samsung’s Galaxy AI may be getting a cross-app intelligence upgrade, à la Google’s Gemini Intelligence and Apple’s Siri AI, according to an Android Authority report. Samsung is working on Galaxy Claw, which could make Galaxy AI more agentic and context-aware across your apps.

Also: Samsung mulls Galaxy AI usage limits and subscription tiers

Currently, Galaxy AI lives inside your Galaxy devices and apps, but its smarts are limited to the apps it’s integrated with. Android Authority reports that Samsung’s Personal Agent Core is at the center of Galaxy Claw, connecting Galaxy AI to compatible apps and services, such as Calendar, Contacts, Messages, Gmail, Gallery, Phone, and Voice Recorder.

Android Authority found code that referred to Galaxy Claw in Samsung’s Personal Agent Core app, suggesting that Galaxy AI can complete cross-app tasks. For example, take the request: “Remind me to buy Mom a birthday card two days before her birthday.” An assistant without access to multiple apps will set a reminder to buy Mom a birthday card, but you might have to manually enter the date and time for the reminder to notify you.

With a more agentic assistant, it can access Mom’s contact card and her birthdate, calculate two days before her birthday, and remind you on that date. Like Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI, Personal Agent Core will need special permissions to access your sensitive information, such as messages, photos, and calls.

Also: 4 ways Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector

Android Authority also reports that code strings in the app point to a recurring, scheduled tasks feature, which would allow users to create custom automations and determine how often Galaxy AI should execute them, similar to Apple’s revamped Shortcuts.

Other code strings reveal a Daily Brief, Device Cleaner, Travel Planner, and a widget. An AI-powered daily brief is something I’ve been yearning for as an iPhone user. If I want a Siri-created brief, I’d have to build it via Shortcuts.

Gmail features a Gemini-powered daily brief, which compiles information from my email inbox and GChat messages to show me things I may have missed. I find it very useful for work, since my inbox is flooded and I often miss important emails.

Also: I’m a ChatGPT power user, but I won’t give it my wallet

Samsung’s Galaxy ecosystem includes smartphones, smartwatches, smart rings, earbuds, and tablets, so there are plenty of opportunities for a more agentic Galaxy AI to bridge gaps across the devices in your personal ecosystem.

Additionally, Google Gemini integration is sweeping across Android (and iOS) apps, which might prompt Galaxy users to choose the more robust AI assistant over Galaxy AI. If Samsung can find ways to make Galaxy AI more useful and exclusive to Galaxy users, it might win some people over. However, reports say Samsung is testing subscriptions for heavy Galaxy AI users, so more Galaxy AI integration might incur a fee.

#3035. CNET Survey: $75 Billion in Holiday Packages Could Be Vulnerable to Lurking Porch Pirates

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

The average package value nears $300, yet 20% of US adults don't use security devices to help protect their deliveries due to costs.

Imagine patiently waiting for the special-edition Legend of Zelda Nintendo Switch 2 console or the new iPhone Duo to be delivered to your door — only for it to disappear seconds after arrival. That’s the risky reality we’re facing this holiday season because of porch pirates.

Online holiday shopping has become the go-to way for many US adults to conveniently find, compare and buy must-have gifts. But leaving those pricey gifts at your door gives thieves a better chance of snagging them in seconds if you don’t have a plan to store them out of sight.

CNET’s annual package theft survey polls US adults about their experiences with porch pirates and how they try to prevent it. This year, the average package value is close to $300, and 28% of US adults have had a package stolen, know someone who has or caught an attempted theft within the past year. Yet 20% of US adults don’t use security devices due to hardware costs or monthly subscription fees.

But leaving your packages unguarded could be a big risk — especially during the holidays. On the other hand, bad actors have been caught in the act on home security cameras. Is it really enough to deter bad actors, and what more can you do to protect your deliveries?

CNET’s findings show that some US adults have dealt with porch theft firsthand: 8% had packages meant for themselves or their households stolen within the past year, and 5% had a delivered gift stolen. Very few (1%) caught a theft in the act on a video doorbell or security camera.

Meanwhile, many US adults know someone who fell victim to package theft — 13% know a neighbor or community member who had a package stolen within the past year, and 12% know someone who doesn’t live in their community who has.

“Close to a third of our respondents are personally acquainted with package theft, which is still a high number compared to other issues like break-ins,” said CNET’s senior home security editor, Tyler Lacoma. “Thieves generally look for crimes of opportunity, and few things are easier than a package left on a doorstep, especially if nobody is home.”

Surprisingly, most US adults (72%) haven’t experienced package theft or know anyone who has.

Even though the percentages above may seem low, Lacoma said that package theft typically increases during the holidays when thieves know more deliveries are likely, and new porch theft tactics are always on the horizon.

There are reports of thieves trying Wi-Fi jamming to disable live security camera footage while they steal packages. And findings show that some are installing spy cams in high-value neighborhoods to learn your home’s layout and habits to take your packages shortly after they’re delivered. In recent years, pirates have even tracked shipping labels for high-value tech, like iPhones, to steal the package within minutes of arrival.

So while the majority of US adults haven’t fallen victim, that shouldn’t be a sign to shrug off the concern or relax your home security measures. Instead, now’s the time to plan how to safely store your packages if they’re delivered while you’re away.

Online shopping and deliveries to your door can be a convenient way to check off holiday wish lists, but the average package value this holiday season is less than last year. CNET found that US adults plan to have an average of $276.24 in holiday packages delivered during this holiday season. That’s $23.82 less than last year’s average of $300.06.

By generation, Millennials also have a lower estimated average package value than last year, with an average of $227.25, compared to their 2025 package value of $307.47 — an $80.22 difference, while Gen Z’s package value is only about $7 less than last year. But any package’s value is still worth taking precautions to help prevent it from being stolen.

Lacoma has thoughts on why that might be. In short, lower spending could mean fewer packages.

“I wonder if people have also simply gotten fewer packages in general this year due to tariffs, inflation and tech prices. That could pull these numbers down,” said Lacoma. But there’s a high chance that could be the case considering CNET’s 2026 annual holiday survey, which found that US adult tech spending is down to $808 — which is $123 less than last year’s average of $931.

Thieves may not always know what’s in boxes they’re stealing but they’re willing to take a chance. We asked US adults which items were stolen in package thefts in the past year to give you a sense of what’s at risk.

Among the items stolen, apparel and accessories were the most common goods stolen (40%). That’s followed by toys and games (23%). Then there are everyday home basics, like decor, cookware and small appliances (19%).

But personal tech devices and accessories are still among the items stolen. Small accessories like phone chargers and cases are most common (16%) among tech-related packages stolen. They are followed by audio gadgets like headphones and Bluetooth speakers, along with streaming devices and soundbars (11%, respectively).

Still, more costly tech like gaming consoles (10%), computers and laptops (9%) and smart home devices (6%) are among devices stolen.

You shouldn’t leave your packages up to chance. That’s why Lacoma recommends a few safer options to ensure your packages are stored securely after they’re delivered, even beyond keeping an eye on your doorbell or security camera. Instead, keep your packages out of sight with tactics like a delivery box with a code or key or ask for an in-garage delivery.

“Delivery boxes have reached a new level of popularity in recent years as an effective way to stop porch pirates completely. However, Amazon’s Key service that delivers to your garage is an alternative,” said Lacoma. “Either way, you’ll need to trust delivery people to handle your shipments, unless you want to arrange for pickup at a nearby shipping center, which some people like to combine with other holiday errands.”

If you don’t want to install a new security feature, try scheduling your packages to arrive when you know you’re home, requiring a signature from someone you trust or changing your delivery location to a pickup spot, like UPS’ Hold for Pick-Up locations or Amazon Lockers.

Home surveillance, like outdoor security cameras and video doorbells, can deter package thieves who don’t want to risk getting caught on camera. But US adults have mixed feelings about their effectiveness in protecting against package theft.

“Fortunately, the right home security picks can solve both these problems,” said Lacoma. “Brands like Tapo, Eufy, Aqara and even Google Nest offer package detection and alerts for free, so you don’t have to worry about extra fees.”

Among all US adults, only 14% have security devices with a monthly subscription that lets them save or playback video. By comparison, 12% have security devices but no subscription.

Those percentages could be low for a few reasons, including the overall perception of how helpful surveillance and security really are against porch theft. Eleven percent of US adults don’t think security devices deter porch thefts. It’s a valid concern since 4% fell victim to package theft or an attempted theft despite having security devices. And some US adults (9%) use security devices to get proof of a theft after the fact — not to prevent it.

But that doesn’t mean you should ignore the possibility of package theft — especially during the holidays. Even if you don’t want to install cameras or new security devices, make a plan to protect your packages and avoid the headache of package theft over the holidays.

“Remember, the simple presence of a security camera is enough to make many thieves look elsewhere – interviews have confirmed it,” said Lacoma. “And with today’s phone alerts about package detection, you can usually check on a package only seconds after it appears, or bring up footage if it unexpectedly vanishes, letting you take action fast. New practices like delivery boxes or in-garage delivery help address risks in concrete ways, too.”

CNET commissioned YouGov Plc to conduct the survey. All figures, unless otherwise stated, are from YouGov Plc. The total sample size was 2,016 adults. Fieldwork was undertaken between Oct. 23–27, 2026. The survey was carried out online. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all US adults (aged 18 plus).

The $75 billion figure was calculated by multiplying the average value of deliveries each US adult expects to receive by the 2025 US population of adults ages 18 and over calculated by the US Census Bureau.

Viking (VIK +4.43%) reported total revenue of $2.2 billion for the third quarter, representing a 9.2% increase driven by fleet expansion and higher revenue per Passenger Cruise Day. Management noted that historically low water levels on European rivers impacted financial results, leading to an estimated $100 million reduction in both revenue and Adjusted Gross Margin. The company issued $265 million in goodwill vouchers to affected guests who traveled during the disruptions. Management stated that 68% of capacity for the 2027 core products is already booked, representing $5.8 billion in advance bookings.

Operator: Good morning. My name is Tom, and I will be your conference operator today. At this time, I would like to welcome everyone to Viking's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. As a reminder, this call is being recorded. [Operator Instructions] I would now like to turn the program to your host for today's conference, Vice President of Investor Relations, Carola Mengolini.

Carola Mengolini: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Viking's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call.
