#2948. Nauticus Robotics (KITT) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Management weighed UAE expansion delays against growing defense demand.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Nauticus Robotics (KITT -17.70%) reported third-quarter revenue of $2.2 million and a net loss of $4.9 million while executing three offshore wind and subsea cable projects. Management highlighted the extension of debt maturities and efforts to maintain NASDAQ listing compliance. The company is establishing a manufacturing and operations center in the UAE and integrating its ToolKITT software into existing ROV systems. Strategic focus remains on the defense market, specifically autonomous underwater systems for mine countermeasures and infrastructure protection.

Operator: Hello, everyone. Thank you for joining us, and welcome to the Nauticus Robotics, Inc. Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. [Operator Instructions] I will now hand the conference over to Kristin Moorman, Corporate Development Lead. Kristin, please go ahead.

Kristin Moorman: Thank you, and good morning, everyone. Joining me today and participating in the call are Jimena Begaries, Interim CFO; Jason Close, Go-to-Market Lead; and other members of our leadership team. John Gibson, CEO and President, should be joining us for the Q&A session. On today's call, we will first provide prepared remarks concerning our financial and operations results. Following that, we will answer questions. We have now released our results for the quarter ending September 30, 2026, which are available on our website. In addition, today's call is being webcast, and a replay will be available on our website shortly following the conclusion of the call.

Please note that comments we make on today's call regarding projections or our expectations for future events are forward-looking statements. Forward-looking statements are subject to a number of risks and uncertainties, many of which are beyond our control. These risks and uncertainties can cause actual results to differ materially from our current expectations. We advise listeners to review our earnings release and the risk factors discussed in our filings with the SEC. Also, please refer to the reconciliations provided in our earnings press release as we may discuss non-GAAP metrics on this call. I will now turn it over to Jimena.

Jimena Begaries: Good morning. Thank you, Kristin, and thank you to everyone for joining us today. During the third quarter of 2026, we successfully extended the maturities of our outstanding debt obligations, providing additional flexibility as we continue to advance operations and commercialization efforts. We also maintained compliance with NASDAQ stockholders' equity and continued listing requirements, which remains an important priority for the company. We are actively planning in the event that rule changes so that we can sustain our listing. I will now discuss our financial results for the third quarter of 2026. Revenue for the third quarter was $2.2 million, an increase of $1.4 million sequentially and an increase of $0.3 million compared to the same quarter last year.

Operating expenses for the quarter were $6.5 million, a decrease of $1.4 million from Q3 2025 and a decrease of $0.4 million sequentially. This reflects a continued focus on cost management, partially offset by increased activity levels compared to the first quarter of 2026. G&A costs for the quarter were $2.7 million, representing an improvement of $0.3 million from the same quarter last year. Sequentially, G&A has decreased $0.6 million, demonstrating continued discipline in managing our corporate overhead. Net loss for the quarter was $4.9 million compared to $11.1 million in the second quarter of 2026 and $6.6 million in the third quarter of 2025.

This decrease was driven mostly by noncash losses recognized on debt extinguishment transactions related to the exchange of outstanding debt for equity securities during Q2. Adjusted net loss for the quarter was $5.3 million compared to $6.8 million in the third quarter of 2025 and $6.9 million in Q2 of 2026. Cash at the end of Q3 2026 was $5.6 million compared to $7.6 million at the end of 2025. This decrease is related to cash used in operating activities, slightly offset by raises from our At-the-Market facility. The progress made during the third quarter, including improved operating performance and the extension of former debt maturities provides a stronger foundation as we continue to execute our strategy.

With that, I will now hand the call over to Steve Walsh, our sales lead, for an update.

Steve Walsh: Thank you, Jimena, and good morning. As we reflect on the third quarter, Nauticus Robotics continued to execute its strategy with a focus on operating efficiency, customer relationships, and expanding opportunities across our commercial, technology, and defense businesses. During the third quarter, Nauticus generated $2.2 million in revenue, reflecting strong operating activity while maintaining disciplined cost management and operating margins. Our flexible operating model continues to deliver expected cost savings by aligning personnel and equipment with specific project requirements rather than maintaining a fully mobilized vessel throughout an entire work season. This approach allows us to manage costs more effectively, maintain operating efficiency and match resources to customer demand while preserving flexibility to pursue additional opportunities.

Turning to offshore wind and subsea cable laying. We supported 3 projects during the quarter, including 2 with existing customers and one that introduced Nauticus to a new client. We have just completed a cable-lay project offshore California while also pursuing another West Coast project that could begin in December 2026 and extend into January 2027. Internationally, we are advancing discussions toward potential negotiations for an extended duration project that could extend into 2027. Our ability to offer competitive mobilization costs and efficient project execution supports our efforts to expand internationally and diversify our revenue opportunities.

An important strategic priority is expanding our portfolio of larger, longer-term contracts that provide more predictable revenue streams, strengthen our financial positions and reduce reliance on individual project awards. Securing these engagements will help to create greater operational and financial stability while providing continuity during seasonal periods of offshore activity. Our technology business also made meaningful progress. Nauticus ToolKITT has been successfully integrated into the Comanche ROV system and continues to deliver excellent results. The integration demonstrates the value of combining subsea robotics with intelligent software to improve vehicle stability, operational efficiency and the quality and consistency of data delivered to customers. These capabilities can also help to reduce unnecessary vehicle wear and support increasingly autonomous subsea operations.

Importantly, utilizing Nauticus ToolKITT in our own operations is generating additional real-world operating hours, accelerating technology development, and allowing us to refine and commercially harden our solutions. This provides an opportunity to demonstrate performance, reliability and commercial value under actual operating conditions while advancing the technology for broader customer applications. We have also continued to advance our business development and efforts in the defense market. Given the range of activities and opportunities under consideration, our defense business development lead will provide a separate update on these efforts and Nauticus' future positioning for the future opportunities.

Looking ahead to 2027, our priorities are to execute successfully on awarded projects, maintain operating discipline, expand our offshore wind and subsea cable-laying activities, advance international opportunities and continue developing our commercial defense technology applications. Our flexible operating model and technology platforms provide a foundation for pursuing growth across multiple markets while maintaining a focus on operational performances and capital discipline. In summary, the third quarter demonstrated our ability to generate meaningful revenue, operate efficiently, strengthen customer relationships, and advance technology with tangible operational benefits. We are encouraged by the opportunities ahead and focused on converting our commercial pipeline and technology progress into sustainable growth. We appreciate the continued support of our shareholders, customers, employees and partners.

We remain committed to executing our strategy and creating long-term value for our shareholders. With that, I'll turn it over to Tyler Guice, our defense lead, for an update on our government discussions.

Tyler Guice: Thanks, Steve. Good morning, everyone. It's a pleasure speaking with you today. Over the past quarter, Nauticus Robotics has made significant progress in what we believe represents one of the most important opportunities in our company's history, the growing market for autonomous underwater defense systems. To appreciate why we're excited, it's important to understand where Nauticus began and how the defense market has changed. When Nauticus was founded, we recognized the potential of autonomous underwater robotics for both commercial and military applications. At the time, AV investment was largely focused on early-stage engineering and development programs dominated by major defense contractors. These programs required substantial capital, extended development time lines, and considerable financial risk.

We made the strategic decision to concentrate on commercial applications, particularly offshore energy, while continuing to develop and mature technology. That decision positioned us for the opportunity we see today. Over the ensuing years, we advanced Aquanaut and our proprietary Nauticus ToolKITT autonomy technology through engineering, integration, and testing. Today, we have a substantially more mature technology offering. And importantly, the defense market is moving in our direction. Growing geopolitical uncertainty, threats to critical subsea infrastructure, and the increasing importance of maritime security are accelerating demand for autonomous underwater capabilities. The Navy is placing greater emphasis on higher technology readiness level systems that can be evaluated and transitioned toward operational use more rapidly.

Nauticus is no longer approaching this market with a concept requiring years of development. We're bringing an existing robotic platform with demonstrated capabilities. Aquanaut combines broad area survey, close inspection, sensor integration, underwater communications, and autonomous operations in a single platform. We believe this combination is particularly relevant to mine countermeasures, seabed security, and critical infrastructure protection. Importantly, underwater robotics and autonomy are not peripheral businesses for Nauticus. They are the foundation of our company. Our specialization and integrated capabilities distinguish us from many participants in the defense market. During the quarter, we expanded our engagement with the U.S. Navy, allied naval organizations and established defense contractors.

Our participation in defense conferences in Washington, D.C. and Portugal provided direct access to military leadership and industry decision-makers. What is particularly encouraging is that these discussions are progressing beyond introductions towards specific operational requirements, technical evaluations, and potential acquisition pathways. We are also exploring partnerships with established defense contractors that can integrate our technology into larger defense programs. Our ambition is not simply to supply underwater robots. It is to become an important technology partner in autonomous subsea defense. The Navy's growing investment in autonomous and unmanned systems reinforces our confidence in this opportunity. And there is another important consideration for shareholders. We've already invested years of engineering, integration, and testing in these technologies.

We now have an opportunity to leverage that investment in the defense market increasingly seeking mature operationally relevant solutions. Our priority is execution, advancing these engagements into demonstrations, strategic partnerships, funded programs, and ultimately sustainable revenue. We recognize that defense procurement requires time and discipline, but the opportunity today is fundamentally different from the one Nauticus first encountered. This is not a departure from our original vision. It is an opportunity to realize that vision in a market increasingly ready for what we have built. We believe defense can become a significant driver of Nauticus' long-term growth. We've spent years preparing our technology for this moment. We believe the market is now moving toward us.

Nauticus intends to be a meaningful part of the future of subsea defense. I'll now hand you over to Ameen, our engineering lead, for an update on product progress.

Ameen Albadri: Thank you, Tyler. Our continued focus on defense application is driving the advancement of Aquanaut's capabilities to meet evolving mission requirements. Establishing our manufacturing and operations center in the UAE will play a key role in supporting these efforts by enabling us to design, manufacture, and deploy multiple mission-ready Aquanaut vehicles for defense and commercial demonstrations. We have made meaningful progress toward establishing this regional hub. The facility has been selected, and we are currently finalizing the required regulatory approvals. This expansion will strengthen our regional capabilities, improve our ability to respond to customer needs and support future growth in the Middle East and beyond.

Over the past 2 years, we have made significant progress in transitioning Aquanaut from an advanced development platform into a commercially capable subsea system. As a result, we are entering the defense market with a mature technology platform that is capable of demonstrating a broad range of mission relevant capabilities and can be further adapted to meet evolving defense requirements. More recently, we have focused on advancing Aquanaut's mine countermeasure capabilities, leveraging its current capabilities to support mine detection and identification missions. Our active engagement with defense organizations and potential customers continues to play an important role in guiding our development efforts.

These relationships allow us to better understand operational requirements, validate our technology against real-world mission needs, and continue refining our software and autonomous capabilities. At the same time, we see these advancements as building a foundation for broader commercial applications. As we continue to mature the Aquanaut platform and demonstrate its capabilities in an increasingly demanding environment, we believe there will be meaningful opportunities to expand these services into the offshore energy market and other sectors. Development of our next-generation fully electric manipulators also continues to progress with ongoing prototype testing and software development. We have implemented several design and functional improvements in preparation for in-water testing and integration with Aquanaut.

Establishing manufacturing capabilities in the UAE will help accelerate this program and support the transition from prototype development toward production. Our long-term focus remains on differentiating Aquanaut through advanced autonomous manipulation, payload deployment, and close-range inspection capabilities, enabling the vehicle to execute increasingly complex underwater missions. The integration of these capabilities with our autonomous technology remains central to our development road map, strengthening Aquanaut's competitive position and expanding opportunities across both defense and commercial markets. I'll now hand the call to Jason.

Jason Close: Thank you, Ameen. As we close today's prepared remarks, I want to bring together a few important developments across our business and share some of what we're seeing firsthand in the market. First, as you've heard from Jimena and Steve, we had a strong quarter of ROV operations, executing a significant amount of offshore work across multiple projects and customers. We're also seeing the benefit of Nauticus ToolKITT in these operations with improvements in vehicle performance, consistency, and the quality of work delivered to customers. But what I really want to focus on today is the momentum we're seeing in the defense and international markets.

I've spent much of my career bringing new technology to market, and I can count on one hand the number of times I've experienced the level of engagement we're now seeing at industry events. Typically, when you're commercializing a new technology, a great deal of effort goes into finding prospective customers, explaining the value proposition, and convincing them that they need your solution. What we're experiencing in defense right now is remarkably different. At recent industry conferences, senior representatives from relevant organizations are actively seeking us out. They're coming with specific operational challenges, clear requirements, and a genuine urgency to identify solutions.

In many cases, we're not having to convince them that the problem exists or that autonomy is part of the answer. They already know that. Importantly, we're consistently hearing that Nauticus is ahead of many of the alternatives they're evaluating in terms of technology readiness and actual operational experience. That's an important distinction. There are a lot of companies talking about what autonomous underwater systems might eventually do. We've already built and operated highly capable subsea robotic systems, and that operational maturity is resonating with customers seeking solutions they can move towards deployment. I don't want to understate how unusual this level of market engagement is.

In my experience, when customers start actively seeking out a technology provider with this degree of urgency and specificity, it's a very strong indicator that the market is ready to move. Seeing similar momentum internationally. I just returned from the United Arab Emirates, where I attended ADIPEC and spent time meeting with potential customers, strategic partners and regional stakeholders across both commercial and defense markets. What was particularly encouraging was how quickly these discussions moved beyond general interest in our technology. We're already receiving requests to quote potential work, discussing opportunities to position an Aquanaut vehicle in the region and engaging with organizations that are actively looking for ways to help us accelerate market entry.

During my time in the region, I also spent considerable time in Ras Al-Khaimah, meeting with senior leadership and further advancing our relationship with Master Investment Group. These conversations were focused on execution, establishing our regional presence, developing the business, and leveraging regional relationships to identify and access quality commercial and defense opportunities. I had the opportunity to personally visit the facility we are planning to lease from our regional manufacturing and operations center. Seeing the facility firsthand reinforced my excitement about establishing a real operational presence capable of supporting our business across the UAE and broader GCC region.

What stood out to me throughout the trip was the level of engagement and the willingness of regional stakeholders to help us move forward. The conversations weren't simply about the potential of our technology. They were about identifying the right opportunities, making the right connections, and what it will take to get Nauticus operating and delivering in the region. Just as we're hearing in the defense markets elsewhere, we're hearing consistent feedback about the maturity of our technology and our operational readiness relative to other solutions. I return from the UAE convinced that we have an opportunity to build a significant regional business. And importantly, we're now having the conversations about customers, infrastructure and execution needed to make that happen.

Across both defense and international markets, we're seeing a meaningful shift in our commercial engagement. Customers are approaching us with defined requirements, requests for pricing and an urgency to move towards deployment. We recognize that shareholders want to see this momentum translate into results, and so do we. Our focus is on converting these opportunities into funded programs, product deployments, and sustainable revenue. We believe the combined -- the combination of growing market demand, the readiness of our technology and our expanding customer relationships puts Nauticus in a strong position to capitalize on the opportunities ahead. Thank you to our employees, customers, partners and shareholders for your continued support. With that, operator, I'd like to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Your first question comes from Peter Gastreich with Water Tower Research.

Peter Gastreich: Thanks for the update from the team. Just a few questions from me. Starting off on the revenue side, it's great to see the quarterly revenue coming through. Could you break down the drivers there? Is this a level that you think can sustain? And roughly what revenue run rate will get you to cash breakeven?

John Gibson: Peter, it's John Gibson. The revenue was stronger, and we had more opportunities in more diverse markets. There's still opportunity for us to increase the utilization of the current ROVs that we have. And so there's upside in the revenue from the ROV division, and we continue to work on that. When you speak of cash flow breakeven, I'll try to address that. I think what's really important and what we're working on diligently is the software sales as that has the greatest margin for us, and it gives us the opportunity on lower revenues to produce more earnings. And as a consequence, that's a lot of our focus at the moment as well as the Aquanaut itself.

The enthusiasm we have in the defense industry presents some opportunities for us that we'll be discussing probably in the next call that we have at the end of Q4, as we're putting out the K, we think there are some really good opportunities that are beginning to materialize on the defense sector, particularly associated with mine countermeasures. And it's more than just a vehicle. It's also the software that's driving the vehicle and how the vehicle behaves and its capabilities compared to competitors. I think we're in a really unique position.

And it's going to be moving that -- the Aquanaut into the defense sector where there are longer-term opportunities instead of the tactical ones that we look at with the Aquanaut for smaller short-term, higher cost services. And then the ROVs, it's taking advantage of the market that we have there for them and just getting the utilization up, maintaining discipline on the cost side. But I think it's those -- the combination of those 3 things together are what will get us to cash flow breakeven and I'm not really prepared to make a projection on that on the call, Peter.

Peter Gastreich: Okay. All right. And so regarding backlog heading into next year, is that an area you're able to provide any color? Or how would you characterize the pipeline coverage when compared to, for example, this time last year?

John Gibson: I wish I had a large backlog number to share with you, so we can see the stock climb today. But we -- our tendency is still be in tactical mode. So we're in call-out work. So it means we have to be engaged fully every day with customers and prepared to put equipment in the field as quickly as we can in order to catch the work. And then what the good part of our operations are the success and the quality of the services that we're rendering are causing us to be held out. So if we get on a job, we're often called to extend that job for additional days.

And so that -- we still are in the, I would say, the tactical market as opposed to the strategic long-term market, and that is the shift that Steve mentioned in his comments that we're working towards securing longer-term contracts that allow us to do better planning and better cost management. But the amount of backlog, not -- we don't really have a number that we'd like to put out today.

Peter Gastreich: Okay. Great. So on the UAE, you've selected Ras Al-Khaimah facility there, and mentioned that you're finalizing approvals. What's left on that side? And what would be the road map to that facility sort of being up and running with that Master Investment Group?

John Gibson: Ameen, do you want to comment?

Ameen Albadri: Yes. Next step is once we get the regulatory approvals and we start establishing our manufacturing and operations center in there. We were looking to work with the local talent to hire and start working both in the design, manufacturing and also operating Aquanaut. We do have, like, sales that Jason mentioned earlier in the call, we're in contact with multiple customers in the area, and there's a lot of interest for Aquanaut. And so that center will have to be fully established with local talent to support our operation in the area.

John Gibson: It's MIG and Nauticus, we would both agree that we feel like -- had we been there earlier, it would have been there a year ago, would have been much better off. We've had some slowdowns and some difficulties associated with the conflict ongoing in the region that has kept us from ramping up as quickly as we'd like. We are in great hopes that the country will see its way through to get resolution of the conflict and we'll be able to accelerate our opportunities there. But the sweet part of this is that the unrest is causing the demand for the defense applications of the Aquanaut. And so I think we've got the best of both worlds there.

I think things are coming together to where we should be actively working with them in the very near term. Jason, anything on MIG that you wanted to comment on?

Jason Close: Thanks, John. Yes. I think following up on what I mentioned in the general comments, we see a lot of support from MIG. There's a lot of excitement, not just as an investor, but as the opportunities around the UAE for our technology, both in the commercial and the defense space. Clearly, the current conflict increases the urgency around our defense solutions. But we also saw a lot of opportunities around our commercial solutions and servicing the energy industry. And during our trip specifically in Abu Dhabi with Master Investment Group, we were able to speak with a lot of potential customers and the regulatory bodies about enabling and accelerating our entry into the region.

So excited for us to move forward with that.

Peter Gastreich: Okay. I'll just get one more question here before getting back in the queue. Earlier this year, you mentioned that some of the Gulf of America work has -- was slipping into next year because the operators were budgeting conservatively. I'm just curious where those projects stand? And what have you been hearing from customers? What are they telling you about activity on the energy side into next year?

John Gibson: Well, it's a great question, Peter. A lot of the work was slipping as people were getting relief on having to do some of the inspection work, et cetera. And so they were pushing it out further into 2027. There's been a lot of changes in the government, even in BOEM and leadership. We'll see as the new director gets in place as to how they accelerate those programs and get working. Anytime there's a change, there's usually a slowdown. I'd say that we can anticipate acceleration in BOEM performance duties in the Gulf of America in 2027. And we look forward to being a part of that and participating in that.

And most of the work that we're involved in is more of the inspection work more than the maintenance. And so when they're able to delay that work, it's easier to delay inspections than it is actually doing operational maintenance. And so it's -- until we get the manipulators installed on the vehicle and are able to do some of the lighter-duty maintenance work, that's not as big a market for us. I think the manipulators, which we're not talking about on the call, we can make that a topic next time, are progressing extremely well. And I think we'll have one of the only AUVs completely autonomous with manipulators as we go forward into '27.

And we're excited about those and about the opportunity for manufacturing those in Ras Al-Khaimah as well with our partner, Master Investment Group. And so I think the differentiation continues to occur. The vehicle is continuing to mature in ways that make it more and more applicable to multiple markets. And it's -- the Gulf of America itself, though, '27 is probably going to be a really good year, I would say. I think oil and gas prices are strong and will stay reasonably well supported as we go forward and the government itself.

I think as we go through with the changes that have occurred during the election that the focus on the environmental issues will accelerate as we go into '27.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to John Gibson, CEO, for closing remarks.

John Gibson: Well, I appreciate all of you being on the call. It was a good quarter. ROVs were busy. We got out and executed the work really well. We're not having execution issues. We're not having safety issues. We have the right processes in place to be a great company going forward. We've got the right people. And so we're excited about executing with the equipment and engaging in this market. It is an emerging market, and I think we are probably the best positioned company for what the Aquanaut can do. And we are a leader in what the light-duty ROVs can do, given the ToolKITT implementation and the efficiency improvements and productivity improvements there.

It provides us a lot of opportunity. We have a great team in place here, a lot of focus, dedication, and we're going to execute for you. Our goal is to create wealth for shareholders and employees. And so -- and also bring benefit to all our stakeholders, particularly our investment group. We just are thankful for their commitment, and we look forward to speaking to you again when we put out the 10-K.

Operator: This concludes today's call. Thank you for attending. You may now disconnect.

#2946. Top Wall Street analysts recommend these 3 dividend stocks for higher returns

Dividend-paying stocks can enhance portfolio returns by providing a steady income stream to investors and the potential for capital appreciation. Several investors seek exposure to dividend stocks in a volatile backdrop to ensure stable income.

In this regard, recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend stocks, backed by strong financials and cash flows to support consistent dividend payments.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Energy Transfer (ET) is a diversified midstream energy company with about 140,000 miles of pipelines and associated energy infrastructure in 44 states. The company made a quarterly cash distribution of 34 cents per common unit for the second quarter of 2026. At an annualized payment of $1.36 per common unit, ET offers a yield of 6.3%.

Recently, JPMorgan analyst Jeremy Tonet reiterated a buy rating on Energy Transfer stock and slightly raised his price target to $25 from $24. The analyst noted that the company delivered a strong Q2 beat across all key metrics.

Tonet highlighted that Energy Transfer raised its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $18.8 billion-$19.1 billion from $18.2 billion-$18.6 billion, reflecting robust base results and cost optimization. The 5-star analyst added that the company "tightened" its capex to $5.6 billion–$5.9 billion and expects capex above $5 billion annually through 2029, given solid opportunities.

About the Hugh Brinson pipeline, Tonet noted Phase 1 (1.5 bcfd) reaching full capacity by September 1 and Phase II capacity (0.7 bcfd) going online by Q1 2027. The analyst also noted completion of a 14-mile Hugh Brinson lateral in Abilene, Texas, and final stages of talks for an additional 250 mmcfd of Oklahoma power plant demand.

"All in, we see ET well positioned to continue capitalizing on organic growth opportunities across the value chain," said Tonet.

Tonet ranks No. 922 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 9%. See Energy Transfer Financials on TipRanks.

This week's second dividend pick is independent oil and natural gas company Permian Resources (PR). The company declared a base dividend of $0.16 per share for the third quarter, payable on September 30, 2026. At an annualized dividend of $0.64 per share, PR offers a yield of about 2.7%.

Recently, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Permian Resources stock and increased his price target to $27 from $22, citing an improved outlook on oil production growth and operational efficiencies.

The 5-star analyst noted that while PR stock has outperformed its peers so far in 2026, he sees further upside. Mehta is confident about the company's operational improvements and ability to deliver incremental free cash flow per share through the strategic ground game program. He added that the program has completed about $1.05 billion in bolt-on deals this year (as of August 5).

"We see the continued success of PR's ground game as constructive toward future inventory replenishment and increasing working interest over time," said Mehta.

The analyst also emphasized Permian Resources' solid track record of generating growth in free cash flow (FCF) per share. Mehta expects the company's free cash flow per share to grow at a 20% CAGR (compound annual growth rate) from 2025–2028.

Mehta ranks No. 401 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 12.8%. See Permian Resources Statistics on TipRanks.

Moving on to Sempra Energy (SRE), a utility holding company. Earlier this month, the company declared a quarterly dividend of $0.6575 per share, payable on October 15. At an annualized dividend of $2.63 per share, SRE stock offers a yield of about 3.1%.

Recently, Jefferies analyst Julien Dumoulin-Smith upgraded SRE stock to Buy from Hold but slightly lowered the price target to $97 from $101. The 5-star analyst noted that Sempra stock is trading at a price/earnings multiple that is 14% below its electric peers due to concerns about Texas transmission capital expenditure and the failure of California legislation.

Smith noted that the derating of weaker California peers PG&E (PCG) and Edison International (EIX) is weighing on the sum-of-the-parts (SOTP) valuation but is becoming less relevant given their materially higher fire risk compared to Sempra Energy.

Furthermore, Smith expects Sempra Energy's Texas capex plan to stay in place despite the opposition to transmission and data centers, though delays to 765-kV projects are likely. While a full recovery for SRE stock will need a clearer outcome from the Texas legislative session, Smith believes that the stock may already be an early opportunity for patient investors.

"We are early on the upgrade but see limited downside at current levels as the market is pricing in little transmission upside," said Smith.

Smith ranks No. 945 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 8.2%. See Sempra ETF Exposure on TipRanks.
